title: Agriculture Ministry Denies Kenyan Banana Imports, Contradicts Earlier Reports on Somali Farmers' Struggles
desc: MOGADISHU – Somalia’s Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation has officially denied reports circulating on social media that large quantities of bananas are being imported from Kenya, in a statement that directly contradicts earlier reporting on the issue. In a brief statement issued on Thursday, the ministry dismissed the reports as false and urged the public to rely on official government sources for accurate information regarding agricultural imports. “The Federal Government Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation denies the reports being circulated by some people claiming that Kenya imports large quantities of bananas to Somalia,” the ministry said. Contradicting the Narrative The ministry’s denial comes after widespread social media discussion over reports alleging that bananas from Kenya were being brought into Somalia for commercial sale. An earlier FTL Somalia report claimed that Kenyan bananas were reaching Mogadishu markets by sea without facing the checkpoints, government extortion, or import taxes that continue to suffocate Somali farmers in the country’s historic banana heartlands of Janaale and Buulo-Mareer. That report cited World Bank COMTRADE data showing that Kenya exported $64,000 worth of bananas to Somalia in 2024, amounting to 1,058 kilograms. It also noted that Somalia imported $2.84 million worth of bananas from Ethiopia and Kenya combined, with Ethiopia dominating the market. However, the ministry’s statement now calls these claims into question. Somalia’s Banana Sector: A Complex Reality Somalia is itself a major banana-producing country, with bananas grown in several parts of the country and regularly supplied to markets in Mogadishu and other regions. Janaale in the Lower Shabelle region was previously the centre of a banana production area covering 20,000 hectares. By the early 1990s, Somalia was one of Africa’s main banana producers and exporters.
